articles.author: Tareq El-Ali
articles.description:
The gap


PASETO is a "secure alternative to JWT" — no algorithm-confusion footguns, versioned
panva/paseto.
So there was no maintained JS library that covered both PASETO and full PASERK. That's
paseto-kit fills.
PASETO v4 — XChaCha20 + BLAKE2b (local), Ed25519 (public)
PASETO v3 — the NIST/FIPS-friendly profile: P-384 / AES-256-CTR / HMAC-SHA384
Full PASERK (all 11 types, per version): local/public/secret serialization,
lid/pid/sid key IDs, local-wrap/secret-wrap, password wrapping with Argon2id (v4)
and PBKDF2 (v3), and seal (X25519 / P-384 ECDH)
Registered-claims validation (exp, nbf, iss, aud, sub) with clock tolerance
Runtime-agnostic — one build for Node, Deno, Bun, browsers, edge. No node: imports,
no Buffer; just Uint8Array + WebCrypto's CSPRNG, on the audited @noble/* primitives
import { generateKeyPair, sign, verify } from 'paseto-kit';

const { secretKey, publicKey } = generateKeyPair();
const token = sign(secretKey, { role: 'admin' });
const { payload } = verify(publicKey, token);

Need the NIST profile? Everything's mirrored under a v3 namespace, with distinct key types
import { v3 } from 'paseto-kit';
const key = v3.generateLocalKey();
v3.decrypt(key, v3.encrypt(key, { sub: 'u1' }), { validate: { exp: true } });

Crypto libraries earn trust by being boring and verifiable. paseto-kit implements no novel
test vectors, including the expect-fail cases (e.g. non-canonical
Honest caveat: it's pre-1.0 and has not had an independent third-party security audit.
npm: npm install paseto-kit · repo: https://github.com/Elalitareq/paseto-kit
articles.title: Filling the PASETO gap in JavaScript: paseto-kit (v3/v4 + full PASERK)

articles.author: Antonio Delgado
articles.description:
Every Claude Code session starts amnesiac. Your agent burns 20 minutes discovering
not re-solving solved problems, because it has no memory across sessions
I built AgentPool to close that gap: a shared pool of solved-problem fixes that
Three tools, one feedback loop:
agent hits error ──► ask_pool(problem)      ──► ranked prior fixes
agent solves it  ──► post_solution(p, s)    ──► next agent finds it
agent tries a fix──► confirm_solution(id, ok)──► good answers rise, bad ones sink

Reading needs no auth. Writing needs a free key, minted in-session by a join tool
Each entry is embedded with fastembed (BGE-small, 384-dim, ONNX — no torch) and
sqlite-vec for KNN. A query does cosine top-k, then reranks:
final = similarity*0.6 + normalized(score)*0.3 + recency*0.1
score = Σ(confirm · tier_weight) − Σ(fail · tier_weight)

Every entry and vote is stamped with a provenance tier (anon/free/paid/verified,
With a small pool, k-nearest-neighbor search always returns something —
A shared, writable pool is an attack surface. AgentPoison (NeurIPS 2024) showed a
post_solution runs through a write-time content shield
That shield now also has a second, separate job: a public, writable, human-readable
not a
The pool talks plain HTTP (a cq-compatible REST surface, not just MCP), so
ZugaMind,
agentpool_sync.py
requests, no MCP SDK. Copy-pasteable into
claude mcp add --transport http agentpool https://agentpool-mcp-production.up.railway.app/mcp

Then in a session: "check agentpool before solving this." To contribute:
"join agentpool as " and it mints you a key in-session.
Repo (Apache-2.0, cq-compatible): https://github.com/Zuga-Technologies/agentpool-mcp

articles.description:
Two of the five ways a spend cap can handle a missing price produce the exact same decision stream — same sha256, byte for byte. One of them is the thing everybody calls fail-open. The other is the thing everybody recommends instead of it: fall over to a free local model.
Let me say what that hash is and isn't before it does any work. It covers (seq, label, admitted, charge) and deliberately drops the human-readable reason strings, so two policies that print different words hash the same when they decide the same. Once you see that, the collision is a theorem rather than a discovery: a free fallback charges zero, fail-open charges zero, and a ledger built out of charges cannot tell them apart because there is nothing there to tell apart. The sha256 proves only that my implementation doesn'…

articles.author: Oviawe Nosa
articles.description:
Python’s dominance in AI isn't an accident. In 2026, it’s the center of the modern ML stack because it bridges research, orchestration, and production.
The Ecosystem Advantage
The strongest argument for Python is its mature, battle-tested ecosystem. PyTorch has become the research-to-production backbone, while Scikit-learn remains the gold standard for practical machine learning. These tools let engineers prototype quickly without fighting the language.
LLMs and Code Generation
Large language models have amplified Python’s position. Because Python is highly readable and widely represented in training data, LLMs produce especially high-quality Python code. This creates a feedback loop that accelerates development for AI engineers.
The Nervous System of AI Agents
The biggest shift in 2026 is toward agentic workflows-systems that plan, use tools, and call APIs. If the model is the brain, Python is the nervous system. It’s the connective tissue that lets agents interact with the real world.
Conclusion
Python won’t be replaced anytime soon. Its real power is not that it does everything natively, but that it integrates everything elegantly. It remains the essential language for the future of software.
articles.title: Why Python is the Uncontested King of AI Development in 2026

articles.description:
What happens when you refuse to accept "the source is down" as an answer.
The problem
Every existing scraper I found had the same design: one source, one point of failure. Small HTML change from GitHub → your service is 503 for a week. Rate limited from Cloudflare → same result.
I wanted a trending API that stays up when GitHub's page is down. So I built Hydra, and put it live at hydra9.dev.
The architecture (in one picture)
Why 4 sources and not 2
Track A (github.com/trending HTML): freshest data, but the format changes without warning
Historical data — the thing GitHub won't give you
Hydra runs a Celery beat task every 15 minutes that stores a fresh snapshot to Postgres. That unlocks four analytics endpoints the official page can't offer:
curl https://hydra9.dev/api/v1/trending/new-stars
curl https://hydra9.dev/api/v1/trending/dropped
curl https://hydra9.dev/api/v1/trending/velocity
curl https://hydra9.dev/api/v1/trending/history?at=2026-07-14T00:00:00Z
The stack (deliberately boring)
One lesson: @lru_cache and Pydantic don't mix
@lru_cache
track_singletons(settings: Settings) -> dict[TrackId, Track]:
_. lru_cache needs hashable arguments. Every real request threw:
TypeError: unhashable type: 'Settings'
@lru_cache
Try it
https://hydra9.dev
https://hydra9.dev/docs
https://github.com/loly-baby/Hydra
https://github.com/loly-baby/Hydra
http://localhost:8000/api/v1/trending
